claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.quote: it could be simpler to make JSONErrorReply() do the right thing for 2.0 requests, replacing the Assume with the behavior it asserts
claims.request: Handle JSON-RPC 2.0 errors directly in JSONErrorReply() rather than adding another try/catch block around parse() in httprpc.cpp

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.quote: it seems like this case should get an error reply instead of 204. The JSON-RPC 2.0 spec's examples answer an invalid Request object with no id... with an error and "id": null
claims.request: Consider returning an error reply instead of HTTP 204 for malformed 2.0 requests without an id to comply with the JSON-RPC 2.0 spec, or clarify in test comments that returning 204 is intentional

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.quote: Probably makes sense to update that documentation to say "request body is not valid JSON" instead, to match the behavior after this PR.
claims.request: Update the documentation table in doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md to say 'request body is not valid JSON' rather than 'request parsing error'

claims.author: ryanofsky
claims.quote: The test comments could explain more too. The notification case confused me most: it wasn't clear why {"jsonrpc": "2.0"} fails to parse
claims.request: Expand commit message and test comments to clarify pre-PR behavior and explain why requests without an id fail to parse
